title: A Model Week at the Desk
request: Suppose next week's 500 returns fall into the chutes with the chances in odds. Model one such week with sample_proportions and deliver the modelled number of books in each chute as whole counts.
objective: Simulate one draw from a categorical model and convert proportions back into counts.
hints: The odds say what to expect on average; a modelled week is allowed to disagree with them.
sample_proportions takes the sample size and the array of chances and returns the proportions that actually came up.
Multiply each returned proportion by 500 and round it to a whole count before delivering the array.
inputCode:
import random
from datascience import make_array
flat = [0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 0.1, 0.34, 0.33, 0.33, 0.8, 0.15, 0.05, 0.6, 0.4, 0.0]
start = 3 * random.randint(0, 4)
odds = make_array(flat[start], flat[start + 1], flat[start + 2])
reference:
modelled = sample_proportions(500, odds)
deliver(make_array(*[int(round(share * 500)) for share in modelled]))
